PASSO 1: o gerúndio é uma forma do verbo: STEP 1: the gerund («gerundio») looks like English "-ing", but it does far fewer jobs. It never changes for gender or number, and it shows an action in progress. STEP 2: -ar verbs drop «-ar» and add «-ando»: hablar → hablando. -er and -ir verbs add «-iendo»: comer → comiendo, vivir → viviendo. STEP 3: when the stem ends in a vowel, «i» becomes «y»: leer → leyendo, oír → oyendo, caer → cayendo, traer → trayendo, construir → construyendo, ir → yendo. STEP 4: -ir verbs that change their vowel in the present also change in the gerund: e → i (pedir → pidiendo, decir → diciendo, servir → sirviendo, seguir → siguiendo, sentir → sintiendo, venir → viniendo) and o → u (dormir → durmiendo, morir → muriendo). «Poder» gives «pudiendo». STEP 5: main uses: (a) with «estar», for an action in progress RIGHT NOW («Estoy leyendo»), which you saw at A2; (b) for manner or simultaneity, answering "how?": «Entró corriendo» (He came running in), «Aprendo escuchando música» (I learn by listening to music); (c) for cause, in formal sentences: «Siendo así, no podemos continuar» (That being so…); (d) for condition: «Estudiando más, aprobarías» (By studying more, you'd pass). STEP 6: pronouns attach to the end of the gerund, and a written accent keeps the stress: «dando» + «me» + «lo» = «dándomelo», «diciendo» + «le» = «diciéndole», «hablando» + «le» = «hablándole». STEP 7: with «estar» you can choose: «Estoy hablándole» or «Le estoy hablando» — same meaning. STEP 8: the gerund only describes actions at the same time as, or just before, the main verb. Never a later action: «Salió corriendo» (he ran out), not «Salió de casa llegando a las ocho».

PASSO 1: algumas perífrases (verbo conju: STEP 1: some verb phrases (conjugated verb + gerund) are very common and precise. STEP 2: «llevar» + time + gerund says how long something has been going on — the Spanish for English "I've been studying for two years": «Llevo dos años estudiando español», «Lleva una hora esperando» (She's been waiting for an hour). STEP 3: «seguir» or «continuar» + gerund says something is still going on — English "still" or "keep -ing": «Sigo trabajando en el mismo sitio» (I still work in the same place), «Continúa lloviendo» (It keeps raining). STEP 4: «ir» + gerund says something is gradually progressing: «Voy mejorando» (I'm getting better and better), «La situación va empeorando». Don't confuse it with «ir a» + infinitive (future plans). STEP 5: «andar» + gerund suggests going around doing something, a repeated, often informal activity: «Anda buscando trabajo» (He's going around looking for work). STEP 6: «venir» + gerund is something that has been going on for a while and continues: «Vengo diciéndolo hace tiempo» (I've been saying it for ages). STEP 7: Spanish doesn't accept the gerund as an adjective or for future plans. "A box containing books" is «una caja que contiene libros». "I'm leaving tomorrow" is «Me voy mañana» or «Salgo mañana» — the English present continuous for arrangements doesn't work with «estar» + gerund. STEP 8: English "on arriving", "when leaving" is «al» + infinitive: «Al llegar, llámame» (When you arrive, call me). And actions in sequence are joined with «y» or with finite verbs: «Entró y se sentó».

PASSO 1: o particípio é a forma do verbo: STEP 1: the participle is the form you already use in the pretérito perfecto («he hablado») and in the passive («fue publicado») — English "-ed" / past participle. STEP 2: drop the infinitive ending and add «-ado» (-ar verbs) or «-ido» (-er and -ir verbs): hablar → hablado, comer → comido, vivir → vivido. STEP 3: the irregular ones have to be learned: abrir → abierto, cubrir → cubierto, decir → dicho, escribir → escrito, hacer → hecho, morir → muerto, poner → puesto, romper → roto, ver → visto, volver → vuelto. Compounds follow: descubrir → descubierto, deshacer → deshecho, devolver → devuelto, resolver → resuelto, satisfacer → satisfecho. STEP 4: in compound tenses the participle never changes: «He escrito las cartas», «Hemos visto la película». STEP 5: as an adjective it agrees in gender and number: «las cartas escritas», «una puerta abierta», «los niños cansados». STEP 6: here's an English-speaker trap: positions and states that English says with "-ing" are participles in Spanish. "I'm sitting" = «Estoy sentado» (not «sentando», which means seating someone), "she's standing" = «está de pie», "he's lying down" = «está tumbado», "I'm tired" = «estoy cansado». STEP 7: with «tener», «llevar» or «dejar», the participle agrees with the object and shows a result: «Tengo escritas tres cartas» (I've got three letters written), «Llevo leídas cien páginas» (I've read a hundred pages so far), «Dejó cerrada la puerta» (He left the door closed). STEP 8: the absolute construction uses the participle for a finished action, in writing: «Terminada la clase, salimos» (Once the class was over, we left), «Dicho esto, empezamos» (That said, let's begin), «Hecho el pago, recibirá el recibo». With «estar», the participle describes a state: «La tienda está abierta».
